thread:
jordan_cust: Hey team — running into a weird combo of issues after upgrading our app stack. We upgraded to Node 20 + esbuild and now when we import the Redwood Node SDK in SSR routes we get intermittent 401s from the API and also TypeScript can't find types after bundling. Repro locally with a simple Next.js route.
eli_support: Sorry you're blocked — can you paste your package.json + the exact build command you ran? 401s sound like auth header strip during SSR bundles, types issue might be build output missing .d.ts.
sarah_eng: @jordan_cust can you confirm which SDK version you upgraded to? We recently published a build that has both ESM and CJS entries. Some bundlers rewrite import paths and strip conditional exports. Also curious if you use "module" resolution or any plugin that rewrites imports.
jordan_cust: SDK version is "@redwood/inference-node": "^2.1.0". package.json excerpt:
```json
{
  "name": "customer-app",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference-node": "^2.1.0"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "build": "next build",
    "bundle": "esbuild src/server/entry.ts --bundle --platform=node --outfile=dist/server.js --format=esm"
  }
}
```
When I run the built file locally, API calls from server routes sometimes return 401 and logs show our Authorization header missing. Also tsc after build complains: "Cannot find declaration file for module '@redwood/inference-node'." even though in node_modules/@redwood/inference-node/dist there is index.d.ts before our bundling step.
mike_support: Thanks — can you paste the snippet where you create the client? e.g. new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }) or do you rely on default env reading?
jordan_cust: We do `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-node'` and then on SSR `const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })`. On runtime the env var is present but the outgoing request headers logged by our proxy are missing Authorization on some requests.
sarah_eng: Two possible vector of issues:
- bundler rewrite: esbuild/next can inline or tree-shake conditional exports and sometimes replace runtime code paths used to read env or set headers.
- dual entry mismatch: if the package exposes both cjs and esm and the bundler resolves a lightweight stub that does not include auth middleware, the header could be missing.
eli_support: Would you mind sharing the resolution for that import after bundling? e.g. run `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/inference-node'))"` (for CJS) or inspect the generated dist/server.js to see which module was inlined.
jordan_cust: I ran `esbuild --bundle` and inspected the output. There is a tiny shim that re-exports only `createClient` without the middleware:
```
// excerpt from dist/server.js
var t = function(e){return e};
export { createClient as default } from "./_shim.js";
```
And _shim.js contents are small. Notably no header-attach logic. The original package has a runtime file `lib/node/client.js` that handles headers.
mike_support: ok that does point to the bundler resolving the package to an alternate entry. Can you also run `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('@redwood/inference-node')))"` in a non-bundled env? That will show what's exported normally.
jordan_cust: In non-bundled node it prints `[ 'createClient', 'versions', 'utils' ]` like expected. After bundling it only exported createClient and no side-effect attach code. Also tsc still fails to find types because esbuild replaced the import with an internal path.
sarah_eng: Please try bundling with `--conditions: ['node', 'default']` or set `mainFields: ['module', 'main']` in your bundler config. Esbuild has `mainFields` option via the build API; Next's esbuild pipeline can be trickier.
eli_support: Another quick repro we ask for: a minimal repo. Can you reproduce with a small repo that does `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-node'` and then `console.log(client)` after bundling? If you can share a link or a zip we can run the same bundling command.
jordan_cust: I made a tiny repro: https://example.com/repro.zip (private link) — contains package.json, index.ts that imports createClient and calls `client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })`. Build steps: `npm i`, `npm run bundle`, `node dist/server.js`. After run get 401s.
ops-oncall: tagging runtime team in case there's an API-side rejection pattern. @sarah_eng is the SDK doing any built-time gating that could cause missing middleware when imported via ESM shims?
sarah_eng: No gating in runtime. We do use conditional exports in package.json to point to different builds. Example package.json in SDK:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Bundlers that prefer `import` may pick the esm build which should be fine — but some bundlers inline only named exports and drop module initialization that registers the header middleware if that code path relied on top-level side effects.
eli_support: For the typings issue: ensure the published package has `types` or `typings` pointing to the shipped d.ts in the package root (not nested dist path) and that the files are included in the npm pack. Can you run `npm pack @redwood/inference-node` and inspect the tarball contents?
jordan_cust: Ran `npm pack` and inside there's `dist/index.d.ts` present. But after esbuild bundle the import path is rewritten and tsc in our app can't lookup declarations. Maybe esbuild inlines the module namespace and tsc can't map it back.
mike_support: Action items I'm doing now:
- Requesting eng to verify SDK package exports and ensure our esm build includes the auth middleware and top-level init. (sarah_eng)
- Ask packaging team to double-check `types` export so consumers using bundlers still get .d.ts mapping.
- Recommend temporary workaround: change bundler to prefer CJS entry: set `mainFields` to `['main']` or set `resolve.conditions` to `['require']` in your bundler so the full CJS runtime is pulled in.
sarah_eng: I'll run a quick internal test against esbuild/next bundling to reproduce. If confirmed, we can publish a patch that merges the header attach into a smaller file or ensure side-effects are preserved with named export wrappers.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: redwood/sdk-patch-headers -> staging
eli_support: @jordan_cust can you try the workaround and report back? If that fixes it we can expedite a patch. Also please share the exact esbuild/next version.
jordan_cust: Tried forcing CJS, that fixed the missing Authorization header. Types still flaky but I can manually reference the .d.ts for now. Thanks for triage — will wait on eng patch.
ops-oncall: Noting for incident logs: this caused a customer-facing auth regression when customers migrated to ESM bundling. Tagging as P2 until patch is out.
eli_support: thanks all — we'll follow up when patch lands. Feel free to DM the repro link to eng if you prefer not to post it publicly.
